notes: SEQN is the unique participant identifier in NHANES. It maps to person_source_value to link all data to the same individual.

Dietary day one sample weight is a survey design weight. It can be stored as an observation with a custom concept for survey weights, or used in analysis without direct OMOP mapping. value_as_number holds the numeric weight.
Dietary two-day sample weight is a survey design weight. Similar to WTDRD1, stored as a numeric observation.
Food/Individual component number is an ordinal identifier for food items within a dietary recall. It can be stored as an observation value.
Dietary recall status is a categorical variable indicating the quality/completeness of the recall. It should map to a standard concept for statuses, but a specific concept_id is not provided here.
Interviewer ID code is an identifier for the interviewer. It can be stored as a string observation or linked to a provider table if interviewers are considered providers.

Breast-fed infant (either day) is a binary variable. Concept_id 45878583 corresponds to 'Breastfeeding status' or similar; a more specific concept like 'Breastfeeding' (concept_id 4075920) could be used with value 'Yes/No'.
Number of days of intake is a categorical variable indicating how many days of dietary data are available. It can be mapped to a standard concept for 'Number of days' if available.
Number of days between intake and household interview is a continuous variable. It can be stored as a numeric observation with a custom concept for 'Days between intake and interview'.
Intake day of the week is a categorical variable. It can be mapped to standard concepts for days of the week (e.g., Monday, Tuesday).
Language respondent used mostly is a categorical variable. It can be mapped to standard concepts for languages (e.g., English, Spanish).
Combination food number is an ordinal identifier for combination foods. It can be stored as a numeric observation.
Combination food type is a categorical/text variable describing the type of combination food. It can be stored as a string observation or mapped to a food concept if available.
Time of eating occasion (HH:MM) is a time variable. It can be stored as a datetime observation (with date set to the recall date) or as a string/numeric time.
Name of eating occasion is a categorical variable (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack). It can be mapped to standard concepts for meal types if available.

Source of food is a categorical variable describing where the food came from (e.g., store, restaurant). It maps to observation with a concept representing the source, but a specific standard concept_id depends on the coded values in NHANES.
Binary variable indicating if meal was eaten at home. Could use standard concepts for Yes/No (e.g., 4188539 'Yes', 4188540 'No') but exact mapping depends on NHANES coding.

USDA food code is an identifier for the food item. It can be stored as a string in observation.value_as_string or mapped to a standard concept if a food ontology concept exists. No direct standard concept_id is provided here.

Grams of food consumed. This is a measurement of mass. The concept_id for 'Grams' would be a unit concept (e.g., 8587) but the measurement concept itself (e.g., 'Amount of food') needs a specific concept_id from the vocabulary.
Energy in kcal. This is a measurement of nutrient intake. The measurement concept could be 'Energy' (concept_id 3004249) and unit 'kilocalorie' (concept_id 8588).
Protein in grams. Measurement concept for 'Protein intake' (e.g., 3004250) with unit 'gram' (8587).
Carbohydrate in grams. Measurement concept for 'Carbohydrate intake' (e.g., 3004251) with unit 'gram' (8587).
Total sugars in grams. Measurement concept for 'Sugars intake' (e.g., 3004252) with unit 'gram' (8587).
Dietary fiber in grams. Measurement concept for 'Fiber intake' (e.g., 3004253) with unit 'gram' (8587).
Total fat in grams. Measurement concept for 'Total fat intake' (e.g., 3004254) with unit 'gram' (8587).
